messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard error (standard deviation of the sampling distribution)**  

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test statistic (i.e., the standard error of the mean) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" but likely they want the standard error or something? They provide sample mean, sample std dev, sample size, population mean. They might want the standard error of the mean: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). That would be 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution under null: same as standard error. So answer ~0.2215.

But the tool is for calculating p-value. We could use it to compute p-value. But question: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". That is ambiguous. Could interpret as standard error of the mean under null. So we can compute that manually. Provide explanation. No need to call function. Just give result.
